title: GT 'Daily Trading Intensity' does not follow the formula the prompt states (it divides by company count)
evidence: The prompt defines 'Daily Trading Intensity = Average Daily Trading Value (2 decimals)'. In the GT, Sheet2_KPIs column E is Average Daily Trading Value divided by Total Number of Listed Companies instead. NASDAQ Jan 2025: RawData!G2 = 123581 and RawData!D2 = 3291, so the GT shows 37.55 (123581/3291) where the formula gives 123581.00. NYSE Jan: 124538.6 vs GT 57.15 (124538.6/2179). HKEX Jan: 13404 vs GT 5.09. All 25 rows of the column break the stated definition, off by a factor of 2,000–3,300. The grader compares the output cell by cell against the reference and scores 0/1 overall. An agent that follows the instruction exactly gets values ~3,000x the GT on a whole graded column, which fails 'correctness' and the overall score.
confirmation: Confirmed: Sheet2_KPIs E2=37.55 (123581/3291), E3=40.66 (132660.2/3263), where the prompt formula gives 123581.00 and 132660.20. The graded column contradicts the instruction.
fix: gt_87_ref_0.xlsx, Sheet2_KPIs!E2:E26 (Daily Trading Intensity): each value replaced with the same exchange-month's RawData Average Daily Trading Value rounded to 2 decimals, as the prompt defines (e.g. NASDAQ January 2025 37.55 -> 123581.00). No other cell changed.

title: Ground truth Sheet2_KPIs 'Daily Trading Intensity' divides Average Daily Trading Value by Total Number of Listed Companies, contradicting the prompt formula
evidence: In `problem.py` (Subtask 1 - Sheet2_KPIs), the prompt explicitly defines the formula for the fifth column as: `Daily Trading Intensity = Average Daily Trading Value (2 decimals).` In `RawData` (Column G), `Average Daily Trading Value (USD millions)` for NASDAQ (Jan–May 2025) is `123581`, `132660.2`, `144910.9`, `161912.3`, `138406.7`. However, in the ground-truth file `gt_87_ref_0.xlsx` (`Sheet2_KPIs`, Column E, rows 2–26), every cell in `Daily Trading Intensity (USD millions)` is instead computed as `Average Daily Trading Value / Total Number of Listed Companies` (e.g., for NASDAQ Jan 2025: `123581 / 3291 = 37.55`; Feb 2025: `132660.2 / 3263 = 40.66`; NYSE Jan 2025: `124538.6 / 2179 = 57.15`; HKEX Jan 2025: `13404 / 2633 = 5.09`). Because the binary (0/1) AI grader rubric (`grader_guidance` -> `2. Data Accuracy`) instructs the judge to verify whether every cell in the model's output is logically equivalent to the reference answer (`gt_87_ref_0.xlsx`), a competent agent following the explicit prompt formula will produce values ~2,000–3,000x larger than the ground truth across all 25 rows and fail the `correctness` and overall `score` checks.
confirmation: The prompt says 'Daily Trading Intensity = Average Daily Trading Value (2 decimals)', but gt_87_ref_0.xlsx Sheet2_KPIs!E2 is 37.55 = RawData G2 123581 / D2 3291, and the rest of the column follows the same division. An agent that follows the stated formula diverges on the whole column.
fix: gt_87_ref_0.xlsx, Sheet2_KPIs!E2:E26 (Daily Trading Intensity): each value replaced with the same exchange-month's RawData Average Daily Trading Value rounded to 2 decimals, as the prompt defines (e.g. NASDAQ January 2025 37.55 -> 123581.00). No other cell changed.
